problem: Use the first three non-zero terms of the Taylor expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ to approximate the value of $\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5}).$ Give your answer to $3$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
We use Taylor's formula in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+⋯,
$$

with $a=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ 

Calculating the necessary derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡x \\ f(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & ={sec}^{2}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=2 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =2{sec}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x \\ {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =2{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Taylor series is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =1+(2)(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{(4)}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+2(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+2{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{5}$ into the above to approximate $\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5}).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5}) & ≈1+2(\frac{\pi }{5}-\frac{\pi }{4})+2{(\frac{\pi }{5}-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2} \\  & =1+2(-\frac{\pi }{20})+2{(-\frac{\pi }{20})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{\pi }{10}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{200} \\  & =0.735\,,\end{aligned}
$$

to three decimal places.
